big_idea: We DESCRIBE positions and MOVEMENTS to navigate a maze. Forward, turn, reach the goal.
learning_intention: We are learning to describe positions and movements on a map.
student_learning_goal: I can describe positions and movements on a map.
success_criteria: I can DESCRIBE position with words.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Symmy and Flippy — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Symmy: Welcome to the MIRROR MAZE! Use directions to navigate. Forward 3, turn right, forward 2 — REACH THE GOAL! Symmy + Flippy open: 'Sort, AREA, CONGRUENT, MAP!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Symmy and Flippy puppets in capes. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use ALL we know: sides + symmetry, compose + area, congruent, maps, AND directions.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write MOVEMENT on chart. 'Movement = going from one place to another. We DESCRIBE with FORWARD, BACKWARD, LEFT, RIGHT + a NUMBER.'

Demonstrate. Show a maze: START at one corner, GOAL at another. 'Forward 3 squares, turn right, forward 2.' Trace the path.

More. Different maze. 'Forward 4, turn left, forward 1, turn right, forward 2.'

Now show the 5 stations:
- Station 1: SHAPES — count sides/angles/symmetry on 3 shapes.
- Station 2: AREA — rearrange 6 tiles, prove area = 6.
- Station 3: CONGRUENT — match 4 pairs.
- Station 4: MAP — read a map, find 3 objects.
- Station 5: MAZE — write 3 directions to navigate the maze.

Each child rotates and records on TEMPLATE.

'Symmy and Flippy say — every spatial detective uses ALL these skills.'

'Welcome to the MIRROR MAZE!'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 5 stations rotation (~5 min each).
Stations 1-5: shapes, area, congruent, map, maze.
Stretch: 'big idea' conclusion at the end.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: counts shape attributes; rearranges tiles; matches congruent; reads map; writes directions.

consolidation.exit_routine: Symmy + Flippy capstone refrain — 'Sort, AREA, CONGRUENT, MAP — Symmy + Flippy show the WAY!' Class chants 3x. Each child shares one checkpoint + the skill they used.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When children navigate the mirror maze using only one prior-day skill — repairing the integration gap
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the mirror-maze capstone, the trap is single-skill fixation — child uses ONLY symmetry (Day 1) OR only the map (Day 4) instead of integrating all four prior-day skills. Battista (2007) on spatial structuring of arrays + Clements & Sarama (2009) on path-following place integrated spatial reasoning as the unit's terminal target.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: SORT by sides + symmetry (L1), AREA conservation (L2), CONGRUENCE testing (L3), top-down MAP (L4) into a mirror maze with all four checkpoints.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Maze station. Child writes: 'forward, turn right, forward'. Partner asks 'how many?'. Child shrugs.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Symmy asks — HOW MANY squares? Without a number, your partner is lost.'

Guide. 'Add a number. FORWARD 3. TURN RIGHT. FORWARD 2.'

Generlise. 'Symmy says — every direction has VERB + NUMBER. Forward 3. Turn right (no number for turn). Forward 2.'

Now practice. Trace path: 'forward 3.' Step 3 squares. 'Turn right.' Right turn. 'Forward 2.' 2 squares.

If still no numbers: provide direction template with 'verb + ___' lines.
common_misconceptions: Turns need numbers. (Repair: turns are angle-only, no number.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child uses only one prior-day skill: explicit checklist (1-2-3-4); child checks all four before navigating.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can articulate skills but skips one: drill 'every checkpoint requires a different lens — sort, area, congruence, map.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child completes maze but cannot articulate which skill at which checkpoint: post-walk reflection — child names skill + checkpoint.
